outcome: No resolution, partial resolution, or bound movement found on the equiconsistency question itself within the window; it remains explicitly described as open (the 'holy grail' of inner model theory) in current sources, contingent on a canonical inner model theory for supercompact cardinals that has not yet been built.
summary: The problem asks whether Con(ZFC + ∃ strongly compact cardinal) implies Con(ZFC + ∃ supercompact cardinal). This is a foundational question in large cardinal set theory, repeatedly described in the literature as the 'holy grail problem' of inner model theory, whose resolution is generally believed to require a canonical inner model theory for supercompact cardinals — a program (Woodin's 'Ultimate-L', and work of Steel, Schindler, Trang, Sargsyan, Neeman and others) that has not been completed. I found no preprint, announcement, or published result in the window (26 Jan 2024 – present) that resolves the question, settles a genuine restriction of it, or moves a bound on it. The closest body of related work is Gabriel Goldberg's Ultrapower Axiom (UA) program: under UA (not a ZFC theorem), the least strongly compact cardinal is supercompact, up to a class of counterexamples identified by Menas — this is offered as evidence toward equiconsistency, but (a) the core UA results establishing this equivalence date to 2018–2020 (arXiv:1810.05058, arXiv:2006.03293), well before the frozen revision, and (b) UA's own consistency with a supercompact cardinal is itself unestablished, so even the pre-2024 result does not settle the stated (unconditional) problem. Goldberg's 2024 paper 'Strongly compact cardinals and ordinal definability' (J. Symbolic Logic/J. Math. Logic 2024) extends Woodin's HOD dichotomy from extendible to strongly compact cardinals — a related structural result, not a case of the equiconsistency question, and it does not touch supercompactness directly. Other 2024-2025 work found (You & Yuan on λ-strong compactness cofinality and 'almost strong compactness'; Goldberg & Thei on cardinal-correct inner models; work on ω₁ strong compactness/supercompactness without AC) addresses adjacent or variant questions — different cardinals, choiceless contexts, or almost-strong-compactness — none of which restricts or settles the ZFC equiconsistency question as stated. The current Wikipedia article on strongly compact cardinals (fetched during this research) still states the conjecture as open and unlikely to be resolved before a canonical supercompact inner model theory exists, with no update reflecting any 2024-2026 development. I searched for any AI involvement in this specific problem and found none; nothing in the space of results (all human, traditional set-theoretic proof work) mentions computer or AI assistance of any kind.
competing_reading: One could argue Goldberg's UA-based equivalence result, though older, remains the most substantive 'progress' on this problem and is still actively cited/re-presented (e.g., in 2026 Warsaw talks) as the best available evidence toward equiconsistency; if a future record wanted to credit ongoing exposition/consolidation of that program as 'progress' in the window, that would stretch the definition, since no new mathematical content resolving or restricting the base ZFC question was produced in the window itself. I judge this insufficient to move the status off 'open'.
what_would_settle_it: Either (a) a full proof, in ZFC, that Con(strongly compact) implies Con(supercompact) [or a proof of an unconditional bound/partial case genuinely restricting the stated question, e.g. an unconditional equiconsistency for some specific strongly-compact-like cardinal below full strong compactness], or (b) completion of a canonical inner model theory reaching supercompact cardinals (the Ultimate-L program or a successor), which the field treats as the expected route to resolution.
